decision.meaning: Accept the existing original definition as ordinary presence at a work, meeting, or scheduled activity. It does not define a register, a sheet, or a crowd count. Oxford and Collins separate this presence meaning from their headcount sense.
decision.example: Accept the retained trainer/session sentence as natural ordinary usage: recording attendance means recording whether participants are present. The recording verb does not change attendance into the name of a paper document. This sentence does not approve every attendance expression elsewhere.
decision.difficulty: Accept B2 as a bounded course editorial placement. The exact noun/POS has B2 evidence in CEFR-J v1.5, and a directly inspected intermediate workplace lesson explicitly teaches attendance policy and absence communication. Their different scopes are retained: neither certifies this exact sense or active mastery. Oxford selected-presence C1 remains a real conflict. B2 is not an automatic clamp of C1, a transfer from attend, or an assumption based on a footer.
decision.historical_boundary: The earlier A2 entry and prior hold remain immutable historical evidence. The new candidate resolves only this content-level review; separate guarded integration and metadata review are still required.
